thread:
maria: Heads-up — since the kernel/driver push last night we've seen a bunch of short ECC/Xid spikes in dcgm-exporter metrics across usw2 and euw1. Lots of alerts firing and immediate clears.

maria: Example: 10x alerts in the span of 2m on the same node, each alert lasts <30s. This is drowning real incidents.

maria: Sample snippet from alert stream:
```
ALERT gpu_ecc_error_high (fired)
  node=gpu-node-34
  count=3 (30s)
  severity=page
  labels: region=usw2
```

ajay: Yep saw that. Oncall had to ignore a noisy burst while a RAID rebuild caused PCI chatter on the host. We should avoid draining on transient bursts.

devon: Proposal: add a lightweight "noise_score" derived in Prometheus recording rules that flags ephemeral bursts. Use variance + burstiness heuristics across cards on the same host and across the last 5m window. If noise_score > 0.7, suppress alerting for 60s.

maria: Love that. Can you sketch the PromQL? Keep it cheap — sums and derivs only.

ajay: Draft PromQL idea (untested):
```
# per-gpu recent spike rate
gpu_xid_rate = sum(rate(dcgm_xid_errors_total{job="dcgm-exporter"}[30s])) by (instance, gpu)
# host-level burstiness: stddev over gpus normalized by mean
host_burst = stddev(gpu_xid_rate) by (instance) / (avg(gpu_xid_rate) by (instance) + 1e-6)
# short-term jump: increase over last 2m
short_jump = increase(sum(dcgm_xid_errors_total{job="dcgm-exporter"})[2m]) by (instance)
# noise_score (0..1) heuristic
noise_score = clamp_max((host_burst * 0.6) + (short_jump > 5) * 0.4, 1)
record: infra:gpu:noise_score:ratio
```

devon: Nice. Also add a cross-region check: if the same metric spikes in >=2 regions for same instance pool, lower noise_score (since global events likely real).

maria: We still need a safe suppression mechanism in the alerting rules. I suggest a Prometheus recording and then a prometheus-alerts rule like: only fire gpu_drained_needed if noise_score < 0.5 AND dcgm_ecc_errors_sum > threshold for 10m. That prevents immediate drains.

ajay: Example alert rule snippet:
```
- alert: gpu_ecc_persistent_errors
  expr: sum_over_time(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[10m]) by (instance) > 20 and infra:gpu:noise_score:ratio{instance=~".*"} < 0.5
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    runbook: |
      If noise_score is low and errors are persistent, follow drain+replace runbook: check kernel logs -> try IO pause -> schedule drain if errors continue.
```

infra-bot: (alert) gpu_ecc_persistent_errors fired on gpu-node-82 in euw1 — infra:gpu:noise_score:ratio=0.12 — persistent.

maria: Good signal. For the suppression window we should bias towards short suppression (60-90s) for noise_score between 0.5-0.8, and full suppress if >0.8. Keep audit logs so oncall can re-open suppressed alerts.

devon: Implementation plan:
- Add recording rules (gpu_xid_rate, host_burst, short_jump, noise_score).
- Add alert rule change with noise_score gate.
- Add exporter labeling experiment: let dcgm-exporter add "local_jitter" metric so we can detect host-level I/O events.
- Add oncall webhook metadata when we suppress so we record suppressed->true in alert manager payload.

ajay: Runbook update ideas: only allow automatic node drain when:
- noise_score < 0.3 AND
- errors sustained > 15m OR error count continues to increase post 1 restart attempt.
Otherwise post a P2 for manual triage.

maria: Also discuss cost: previous approach caused churn (drains) that bumped preemptible replacement and capacity creep. This will reduce unnecessary RMA/slot churn.

oncall-bot: Note: scheduled maintenance window in euw1 at 2026-04-02 03:00 UTC — avoid making sweeping changes in that window.

ajay: Action items:
- Devon to open PR with recording rules + tests (today).
- Maria to update runbook and alertmanager suppression annotations (tomorrow).
- I'll add a small dashboard to visualize noise_score by instance (infra/graphs) before we flip the gate.

maria: Thanks — if we see any false negatives after gating we can lower the gate quickly. Keep the suppression conservative at first. :thumbsup:

devon: PR opened: https://git.redwood.internal/infra/monitoring/pulls/412 — contains test vectors, sample PromQL, and dashboard.

ajay: I'll validate with a synthetic noise generator and run 3 test epochs across both regions. Will report results here.

maria: If tests look good, schedule a canary flip next Tue to enable the gate for non-prod clusters only.

infra-bot: (info) PR 412 merged to staging branch. CI: prometheus-rule-check passed.

maria: Closing loop — keeping this thread for the canary postmortem. If anyone sees suppressed alerts that should have fired, ping me directly.
